ownership: Dedicated installed ESO add-on editor provider, not hardcoded Kubernetes plugin forms. Actual discovery, served versions, RBAC verbs and controller feature flags gate production authoring; schema presence does not establish support.
coverage: PushSecret standalone create/edit and external-write consequences

mapping.identity: Name Input -> metadata.name; locked on edit. Namespace fixed to synthetic preview in this mock; cluster kinds omit metadata.namespace. Production namespace picker belongs to shared destination frame.

SecretStore.Provider picker: spec.provider; one provider only. AWS guided, other providers source-only without conversion

ClusterSecretStore.Allowed namespace: spec.conditions[i].namespaces[]; omitted conditions can allow all namespaces

PushSecret.Existing source Secret: spec.selector.secret.name; same namespace, no data fetch

mapping.Generated child: Read ownerReferences and status conditions as inspect-only context. Parent navigation replaces child edit. No child update/delete/annotation execution is offered. Refresh request is an honest unavailable-action explanation, not a fabricated controller call.

advancedSourceBoundary: JSON syntax is YAML 1.2. Guided subset generates a fresh fixture draft. Exact untouched source equality is exercised. Any manual source change locks Form and Review, retaining raw text including invalid syntax, comments and large integers. This is not a bidirectional AST editor and does not claim unknown-field preservation through guided edits of imported source. No sensitive fixture values, annotations, credential material or data payloads exist in the mock. Do not import credentials.
additionalSourceOnlyPaths: ExternalSecret spec.dataFrom extract/find/generator unions, rewrite, per-row sourceRef, remoteRef version/conversion/decoding/metadata policy, target.immutable, target.template data/type/metadata/engine/mergePolicy
SecretStore other provider schemas, optional session token reference, retry and AWS role chains/session settings
PushSecret spec.selector.generatorRef or selector.secret.selector, multiple destination stores and labelSelector, spec.data metadata and conversionStrategy
safety: Direction badges distinguish pull and push. Visible overwrite/delete/fan-out consequences remain outside help. No provider credentials, resolved values, annotations, PEM or Base64 appear. No live requests, no mutations, no fake reconciliation success. Identity locks do not imply spec fields are immutable; actual admission governs changes. Target Secret immutable is a downstream boundary, not ExternalSecret spec immutability.
componentProposal: No new generic base-ui primitive required. Native HTML illustrates existing base-ui composition; no React components shipped. Operator field rules and source parsing stay in add-on provider.
visualReview: Reviewed every capture via seven contact sheets. Compact 1000x700 frame, 32px fields, persistent footer, 13px body, section navigation. Full-size PNGs remain available. No raw sensitive capture made. web-design-guidelines review: native labels, visible focus, semantic buttons, keyboard help/Escape, focus cycle, dark controls, overflow handling. Remaining limitations: tooltip aria-describedby linkage and full application opener/close lifecycle are not modeled.
limits: Fixture selections and policy values are illustrative, not executable production defaults
Guided AWS subset; remaining provider/advanced variants retain source-only boundary
No server validation, live reference fetching, controller-health or RBAC check
Mock validates missing name/region/mapping only; not full admission or provider semantics
Mode preference persistence not implemented; no draft persistence
No raw sensitive source workflow or credential reveal
Review source uses generated non-sensitive fixture fields only; manual source disables review
Source/Review scroll internally; no real application build or cluster operation was run
